title: Finite-group Hopf algebra and lattice quantum-double sectors

items.title: Explicit finite-group quantum-double data
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional algebraic data for a finite group; no braided-category, modular-functor, topological-field-theory, or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with identity $e$. Let $\mathbb C^G$ be the complex vector space of functions on $G$, with point-mass basis $\{\delta_h:h\in G\}$, and let $\mathbb C[G]$ be the group algebra with basis $\{g:g\in G\}$ and multiplication inherited from $G$. Define the $|G|^2$-dimensional vector space

$$D(G):=\mathbb C^G\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[G],$$

with basis $d_{h,g}:=\delta_h\otimes g$. On basis elements prescribe the bilinear multiplication

$$d_{h,g}d_{k,l}:=\mathbf 1_{h=gkg^{-1}}d_{h,gl},$$

the linear coproduct and counit

$$\Delta(d_{h,g}):=\sum_{ab=h}d_{a,g}\otimes d_{b,g},\qquad \varepsilon(d_{h,g}):=\mathbf 1_{h=e},$$

the unit vector and linear map

$$1_D:=\sum_{h\in G}d_{h,e},\qquad \eta(1):=1_D,$$

the linear map $S(d_{h,g}):=d_{g^{-1}h^{-1}g,g^{-1}}$, and the conjugate-linear map

$$d_{h,g}^*:=d_{g^{-1}hg,g^{-1}}.$$

Every displayed operation extends uniquely by the indicated linearity from the finite basis.

Here a **Hopf algebra over $\mathbb C$** is a complex vector space $A$ with linear maps $m:A\otimes A\to A$, $\eta:\mathbb C\to A$, $\Delta:A\to A\otimes A$, $\varepsilon:A\to\mathbb C$, and $S:A\to A$. Writing $ab=m(a\otimes b)$ and $1_A=\eta(1)$, require $(ab)c=a(bc)$, $1_Aa=a=a1_A$, $(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Delta$, and $(\varepsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=\mathrm{id}=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta$ under the canonical tensor identifications. Require also $\Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)\Delta(b)$, $\Delta(1_A)=1_A\otimes1_A$, $\varepsilon(ab)=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)$, $\varepsilon(1_A)=1$, and $m(S\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta=\eta\varepsilon=m(\mathrm{id}\otimes S)\Delta$, where $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$. A **Hopf $*$-algebra** means such a Hopf algebra equipped with a conjugate-linear involution $*$ that reverses multiplication, fixes the unit, and satisfies $\Delta(a^*)=\Delta(a)^*$ and $\varepsilon(a^*)=\overline{\varepsilon(a)}$ for every $a$, where $(x\otimes y)^*=x^*\otimes y^*$ on $D(G)\otimes D(G)$. 

The group basis of $\mathbb C[G]$ is also taken orthonormal when it is used as a finite-dimensional edge Hilbert space. For a finite edge set $E$, choose a bijection to a finite region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z$ and an enumeration of $G$ by $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, where $q=|G|\ge1$. Then $\bigotimes_{e\in E}\mathbb C[G]$ is the $q$-spin space $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ of the finite local matrix algebra definition, and its operator algebra is $M_{q^{|E|}}(\mathbb C)$. Different finite enumerations change only the basis labels.

items.title: Hopf-* structure of the finite-group double
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional algebra over $\mathbb C$ for the displayed finite-group formulas; no physical or categorical extension is asserted.
items.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and use the basis and structure maps on $D(G)$ displayed in the preceding definition. These maps make $D(G)$ a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over $\mathbb C$. The conjugate-linear operation $*$ is an involution reversing multiplication, preserves the coproduct and unit, and satisfies $\varepsilon(a^*)=\overline{\varepsilon(a)}$ for every $a\in D(G)$.

items.title: Oriented finite-group lattice gauge operators
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional mathematics for group-valued edge labels on a finite cellulation; no empirical realization or perturbative claim.
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with identity $e$, and let $\Sigma$ be a finite oriented cellulation of a closed connected surface. Write $V,E,F$ for its vertex, edge, and face sets. Each edge $a\in E$ has a chosen source $s(a)$ and target $t(a)$. For a configuration $\mathbf g=(g_a)_{a\in E}\in G^E$, the edge Hilbert space is $\mathcal H_\Sigma=\bigotimes_{a\in E}\mathbb C[G]$, with orthonormal configuration basis $|\mathbf g\rangle$.

For $v\in V$ and $x\in G$, put $k_u=x$ if $u=v$ and $k_u=e$ otherwise. Define the vertex gauge permutation $U_v(x)$ on basis vectors by

$$U_v(x)|\mathbf g\rangle=|\mathbf g'\rangle,\qquad g'_a=k_{s(a)}g_a k_{t(a)}^{-1}\quad(a\in E).$$

For a face $f\in F$, choose its oriented boundary walk $a_1^{\epsilon_1}\cdots a_m^{\epsilon_m}$, with $\epsilon_j=1$ when the walk follows the selected orientation of edge $a_j$ and $\epsilon_j=-1$ otherwise. Its based holonomy on $\mathbf g$ is

$$H_f(\mathbf g):=g_{a_1}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots g_{a_m}^{\epsilon_m}.$$

Define the vertex average, face flatness projector, and finite lattice Hamiltonian by

$$A_v:=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{x\in G}U_v(x),\qquad B_f|\mathbf g\rangle:=\mathbf 1_{H_f(\mathbf g)=e}|\mathbf g\rangle,\qquad H_\Sigma:=\sum_{v\in V}(I-A_v)+\sum_{f\in F}(I-B_f).$$

items.title: Gauge averaging and flatness commute
items.physical_scope: Exact finite-dimensional group-valued lattice projector model on a closed connected cellulation; no perturbation-stability or thermodynamic-limit claim.
items.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\Sigma$ be a finite oriented cellulation of a closed connected surface, with vertex gauge permutations $U_v(x)$, vertex averages $A_v$, face flatness projectors $B_f$, and Hamiltonian $H_\Sigma$ defined using the group-element edge basis and oriented boundary holonomies. Then all $A_v$ and $B_f$ are commuting orthogonal projections. The Hamiltonian $H_\Sigma$ is positive and has a nonzero common zero vector for all terms $I-A_v$ and $I-B_f$; hence the finite model is frustration-free with ground energy zero.

items.title: Squared finite-group irreducible dimensions sum to the group order
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-group representation theory over $\mathbb C$; no physical interpretation or empirical premise.
items.statement:
For every finite group $H$, let $\operatorname{Irr}_{\mathbb C}(H)$ denote the set of equivalence classes of nonzero finite-dimensional irreducible complex representations of $H$, where two representations are equivalent if an invertible linear map intertwines their $H$-actions. The **character** of a representation $\pi$ is the function $\chi_\pi(h):=\operatorname{tr}(\pi(h))$. The set $\operatorname{Irr}_{\mathbb C}(H)$ is finite and

$$\sum_{[\pi]\in\operatorname{Irr}_{\mathbb C}(H)}(\dim_{\mathbb C}\pi)^2=|H|.$$

items.title: Irreducible sectors of the finite-group double
items.physical_scope: Pure finite-dimensional representation theory of the explicit algebra $D(G)$; no modular-functor, braided-category, or physical-realization claim.
items.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $D(G)$ be the finite-dimensional complex algebra with basis $d_{h,g}=\delta_h\otimes g$ and multiplication $d_{h,g}d_{k,l}=\mathbf 1_{h=gkg^{-1}}d_{h,gl}$. A finite-dimensional representation of $D(G)$ means a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with a unital algebra homomorphism $D(G)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$; it is irreducible when it has no nonzero proper invariant subspace. For $c\in G$, define its conjugacy class $C_c=\{gcg^{-1}:g\in G\}$ and centralizer $Z_G(c)=\{z\in G:zc=cz\}$. The equivalence classes of irreducible finite-dimensional representations of $D(G)$ are in bijection with pairs $(C,[\pi])$, where $C$ is a conjugacy class, $c\in C$ is any chosen representative, and $[\pi]$ is an equivalence class of irreducible finite-dimensional complex representations of $Z_G(c)$. The representation indexed by $(C,[\pi])$ has dimension $|C|\dim\pi$, independently of the chosen representative up to the corresponding conjugation of the centralizer representation. The sum of the squared dimensions of all these irreducible representations is $|G|^2=\dim_{\mathbb C}D(G)$.

title: Finite-group Hopf algebra and lattice quantum-double sectors — Examples

items.title: The four electric and magnetic sectors of $D(\mathbb Z_2)$
items.physical_scope: Finite algebraic example for $D(\mathbb Z_2)$ and the exact square-torus Pauli-string commutation relation; no general braiding, QFT, or empirical claim.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the stated lattice prerequisite. Let $\mathbb Z_2=\{e,s\}$ with $s^2=e$. Its finite-group double has exactly four irreducible complex sectors, each one-dimensional: the two conjugacy-class labels (flux labels) $e,s$ paired with the two group characters $\chi_\pm:\mathbb Z_2\to\mathbb C^\times$ with $\chi_\pm(e)=1$ and $\chi_\pm(s)=\pm1$. In particular, the nontrivial charge character evaluated on the nontrivial flux is $-1$, equal to the commutation sign for one crossing of a closed primal $Z$ string with a closed dual $X$ string on the square $L\times L$ torus for $L\ge3$.
